name: Baked Prosciutto-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers with Spinach & Tomato Salad

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F). Line two baking sheet pans with aluminum foil and coat with a thin layer of oil; set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small bunch cilantro
15 jalapeño peppers
1 ½ small pkgs grape tomatoes
1 ½ (142 g) pkg baby spinach

instructions.primary_message: Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a large bowl.
Using a box grater, coarsely grate cheddar and cream cheese into the bowl with the cilantro; add spices and mash with a fork or the back of a spoon to combine. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ (227 g) blocks cheddar cheese
1 ½ (227 g) blocks cream cheese
1 ½ tsp cumin, ground
¾ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Halve jalapeño peppers lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)

Using a rounded tablespoon measure, fill each jalapeño half with the cheese mixture. Wrap one slice of prosciutto around each jalapeño half and divide between the baking sheets, cheese-side facing up. (Wipe bowl clean with paper towels and reserve for later use.)
Place jalapeño poppers in the oven and bake until golden and crispy, 18-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp white wine vinegar
1 ½ tsp Dijon mustard
½ tsp salt
3 pinch black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Halve tomatoes lengthwise and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Right before serving, add spinach to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide jalapeño poppers and salad between plates. Enjoy!
